newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends firmer on N. Dakota dryness.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends firmer on N. Dakota dryness.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended firmer but below their midsession highs on concern over persistent dry weather in North Dakota and a lack of hedge-related selling, traders said.

Ongoing dryness in western North Dakota has raised concerns about lower spring wheat yield prospects. USDA Monday said the U.S. spring wheat crop as of Sunday was 69 percent good to excellent, against 72 percent the previous week.
"Everybody up here is concerned about how we've not gotten rain for a while," a MGE trader said. "The cash guys are also talking about how farmer selling has slowed down."

Weather problems have enabled MGE spring wheat to gain sharply relative to its counterparts in Chicago and Kansas City. Traders said that MGE July spring wheat has gained about 30 cents per bushel against KCBT July hard red winter wheat over the last two weeks.

MGE spring wheat settled steady to three cents a bushel higher, with July up 3/4 cent at $4.07-1/4 a bushel. July had been as much as 9-1/2 cents higher earlier in the session but was pressured toward the close by weakness in CBOT grains and soybeans.
